data.long_meaning: Anita is a Sanskrit name derived from the word 'anita', which means 'graceful' or 'pleasing'. This name holds great significance in Hindu mythology, where Anita is considered to be a manifestation of the Goddess Durga. She is the one who grants grace, beauty, and protection to her devotees. The name Anita carries the meaning “Graceful, Pleasing” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Anita usually hope their child will grow to embody graceful, pleasing and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: Anita was a prominent figure in the Hindu epic 'Mahabharata'. She was the wife of Bhishma Pitamaha, the grandsire of the Kuru dynasty. Anita was a devoted wife and a pious woman, who spent her life in prayer and penance for her husband's long life and prosperity of the Kurus.

Anita was also the name of a famous queen in the medieval Chalukya dynasty of India. She was the queen consort of Vikramaditya VI, the last great Chalukyan king, and ruled over the kingdom during his minority. Anita is remembered for her courage and wisdom, and is often depicted as an incarnation of the goddess Lakshmi.
